issue_context.title: Prettier parser doesn't recognize custom file extension with specified syntax
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Prettier does not format files that have non-default extensions.
When a language (e.g. JSONC) is specified in Zed support `Format Document` with prettier.

### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it

When using a file extension other than `*.json` / `*.jsonc` with JSONC language selected, Prettier in Zed does not format the file according to the specified syntax settings.

Related PR: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/13666

### Environment

Zed: v0.160.7 (Zed)
OS: macOS 15.1.0
Memory: 64 GiB
Architecture: aarch64

### Zed.log

<!-- Click below this line and paste or drag-and-drop your log-->
```
2024-11-14T22:26:11.241566+08:00 [INFO] Started default prettier in "/Users/shiny/Library/Application Support/Zed/prettier"
2024-11-14T22:26:11.243877+08:00 [ERROR] Formatting failed: default prettier instance failed to format buffer: error during message '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"prettier/format","params":{"text":"..snip..","options":{"plugins":[],"parser":null,"filepath":"/Users/shiny/Downloads/Untitled (24).custom","prettierOptions":{"useTabs":false,"printWidth":80,"tabWidth":2}}}}' handling: UndefinedParserError: No parser could be inferred for file "/Users/shiny/Downloads/Untitled (24).custom".
2024-11-14T22:26:11.243976+08:00 [ERROR] default prettier instance failed to format buffer

Caused by:
    error during message '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"prettier/format","params":{"text":"..snip..","options":{"plugins":[],"parser":null,"filepath":"/Users/shiny/Downloads/Untitled (24).custom","prettierOptions":{"useTabs":false,"printWidth":80,"tabWidth":2}}}}' handling: UndefinedParserError: No parser could be inferred for file "/Users/shiny/Downloads/Untitled (24).custom".
```
comments: Can you provide a minimal example filename/contents which trigger this behavior?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04270e4a-ee4c-4fa1-8736-46e18559d709)

(example is manually set to JSONC).

Here you go.

I cannot reproduce. My steps:
1. Create a new buffer (cmd-n) with the following contents
```json
{
//this is JSONC
  "key": "value"
}
```
2. Switch the language selector from "Plain Text" to JSONC in the language selector in the status bar.
3. Trigger `Editor::FormatDocument` from the command palette.
Note `//` line is correctly indented.

If I wanted to not have to select `JSONC` from the language selector I could add globs to the `JSONC` `file_types` in settings.json:

```json
  "file_types": {
    "JSONC": ["jc", "somedir/**/**.json"]
  },
```

---

> (example is manually set to JSONC).

Your screenshot shows "Plain Text" -- What did you mean by this?

---
Please be silly-explicit with your instructions for reproduction of what you are seeing.
Truly, explain it like I'm five.

@notpeter - my cursor is in the log buffer, which is plain text. 
The example file is set to JSONC via the drop down.
On my machine, if I open up zed to an untitled buffer and set it to JSONC - it will correctly prettier and format it. No errors.

Run `mkdir ex; echo '{"key":"value"}'> ex/example; zed ex`
Open 'example'. Select JSONC from the drop-down. Select the full buffer. Ctrl - Shift - I to initiate formatting. Prettier fails.

In this screenshot I've left the cursor in the example buffer so you can see JSONC is set, and the error at the same time.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/764763e4-4bd2-4e5f-93b0-bcffbe152dda)
That error is;
```
2025-01-27T11:01:50.994160013-05:00 [INFO] Started default prettier in "/home/z/.local/share/zed/prettier"
2025-01-27T11:01:50.998756838-05:00 [ERROR] Formatting failed: default prettier instance failed to format buffer: error during message '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"prettier/format","params":{"text":"..snip..","options":{"plugins":[],"parser":null,"filepath":"/tmp/ex/example","prettierOptions":{"useTabs":false,"tabWidth":2,"printWidth":80},"ignorePath":null}}}' handling: UndefinedParserError: No parser could be inferred for file "/tmp/ex/example".
2025-01-27T11:01:50.998801667-05:00 [ERROR] default prettier instance failed to format buffer

Caused by:
    error during message '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"prettier/format","params":{"text":"..snip..","options":{"plugins":[],"parser":null,"filepath":"/tmp/ex/example","prettierOptions":{"useTabs":false,"tabWidth":2,"printWidth":80},"ignorePath":null}}}' handling: UndefinedParserError: No parser could be inferred for file "/tmp/ex/example".
```

Version of prettier:
```
/home/z/.local/share/zed/prettier/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs -v
3.4.2
```

Example of how it works with 'anonymous' files with no extension:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c28d45a9-d0ba-4039-be22-6a9c574a94f8)

Perhaps because Zed has to pipe it in or save it with an extension before running prettier over it?

For fun I added a rule to format ex/example as JSONC:
```
  "file_types": {
    "JSONC": ["jc", "ex/example"]
  },
```

However, same pathology, identical prettier errors.

Directly invoking prettier:
```
/home/z/.local/share/zed/prettier/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs  /tmp/ex/example
../../tmp/ex/example
[error] No parser could be inferred for file "/tmp/ex/example".
```

at Jan 26 commit 83141d07e9b41dd816155c658bf5246428b18e44 

Note: you could not reproduce because you had an untitled anonymous buffer - those work for whatever reason.

I'm going to guess that zed doesn't hand _its_ mapping to prettier via the `--parser` argument - which is what you need to do for success:
```
❯ /home/z/.local/share/zed/prettier/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs --parser jsonc /tmp/ex/example
{ "key": "value" }
```
vs:
```
❯ /home/z/.local/share/zed/prettier/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs /tmp/ex/example
../../../../tmp/ex/example
[error] No parser could be inferred for file "/tmp/ex/example".
```

I also have this issue with regular JSON:

- Have a JSON file with an unknown file extension.
- Select JSON as language.
- Run editor: format.

Nothing happens.

review_comments:
Also, this seems not correct: if there's something specifically stated as a parser in settings.json, we have to take that, as a user override.

Am I missing something?
The language setting should be higher than the prettier setting, because the user intent to use that syntax to edit. Ideally the syntax and prettier setting should be synced.
Great, seems like more tests for you to write then, to demonstrate this.
@SomeoneToIgnore can you guide me how to set the language of the buffer in the test? I'm the beginner of Rust 😅

It's not about Rust but barely the API usage:
* init a language and add it to the registry similar to how the test linked above
* https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/f9990b42fa3ef81b53d0b0f42c88836e319758f1/crates/language/src/buffer.rs#L962
Thank you! I will update it in the coming days.
